 Takata PSAN Airbag Inflator Saga Returns With 314,000-Vehicle Toyota and Lexus Recall in the US
 Toyota Motor North America is replacing subject Takata inflators because predictive testing suggests critical propellant degradation 
 Published: 19 Nov 2026, 12:09 UTC 
 By: 
 Mircea Panait 
   11 photos Photo: Toyota 
 The most popular Japanese manufacturer in the US market is recalling a whopping 314,029 vehicles fitted with potentially dangerous Takata passenger airbag inflators. Toyota Motor North America hasn't received any reports of ruptures involving this group of inflators, but nevertheless, these inflators are nearing the end of their operational lifespan. 
 Given the aforementioned, TMNA does not intend to wait for the propellant to degrade beyond safe combustion parameters. Iffy propellant could turn a life-saving airbag deployment into an explosion, risking shrapnel projection throughout the cabin. As of this writing, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has confirmed 28 deaths in the United States of America caused by exploding Takata inflators.
 NHTSA campaign 26V748, which is listed under four numbers by Toyota Motor North America, covers both Toyota and Lexus vehicles produced between model years 2002 and 2017. The manufacturer's recall numbers are 26TB25, 26TA25, 26LB11, and 26LA11. The Corolla accounts for most of the affected population, and it's understandable why.
 Between the sedan and pricier hatchback, the Corolla moved 248,088 units in the United States last year, making it the 11th best-selling nameplate in the country. The Camry sold even more units, with TMNA listing 316,185 for the analyzed 12-month period in the US market.
 Subject compact sedans and hatchbacks were produced for model years 2003 through 2008 to the tune of 232,174 vehicles. Otherwise put, the Corolla accounts for nearly three-quarters of the total population. The 4Runner follows suit with 35,949 units from 2016 to 2017, along with 25,174 units of the 2005 to 2006 model year Tundra pickup truck.
 Photo: Toyota 
An estimated 10,736 examples of the 2005 through 2007 Sequoia are being recalled as well, while Lexus contributes 8,931 units of the 2017 model year GX 460, an estimated 1,064 of the 2002 to 2010 SC 430, and one 2011 model year IS 250. Seriously, one vehicle only! The lone IS compact luxury sedan was manufactured on March 1, 2011, in Japan.
 Per the Part 573 filing with the federal watchdog, Toyota Motor North America is targeting inflators installed either as original equipment or replaced under a prior recall. Newer inflators have more service life remaining, yet all of them continue to be monitored by the Japanese automaker. 73980-24130 and 73980-24140 are the part numbers of the subject inflators.
 Said inflators feature phase-stabilized ammonium nitrate, otherwise known as PSAN, as their propellant. As you already know since the Takata airbag inflator scandal was all over the news, the chemistry can deteriorate after exposure to high absolute humidity and elevated temperatures. Repeated temperature changes can degrade the propellant as well.
 These inflators pose a safety risk because bad propellant burns too violently during airbag deployment. The sealed metal cartridge inside the airbag module, namely the part that holds the propellant, is the part that may shatter and create lots of sharp metal fragments. Blasting outward through the fabric of the airbag, this shrapnel is very dangerous indeed.
 Toyota and Lexus dealers nationwide will replace suspect front passenger inflators or complete airbag assemblies, depending on the vehicle, at no charge to affected customers. Notification letters should arrive in the period from December 28, 2026, through January 11, 2027.
